verdict.rationale: The evidence shows goal-style natural-language tasks (e.g., runs.create with a single prompt) and sessions that can hold multiple runs. It does not document a first-party way to compose repeatable workflows with loops, conditionals, or parameters. Chaining runs in a session or scripting with the Python library are developer building blocks or user-side orchestration, not the workflow-composition capability itself.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can compose repeatable multi-step workflows with loops, conditionals, and parameters instead of one-shot prompts
